uno.title: UNO Guide
uno.goal: Empty your hand before anyone else does.
play: Every player starts with seven cards, and one card is turned over to start the discard pile.
On your turn, play a card that matches the top card by colour or by number.
Action cards change the flow: Skip jumps over the next player, Reverse flips the direction, and Draw Two makes the next player pick up two cards.
A Wild card can be played anytime and you choose the next colour; Wild Draw Four also hands the next player four cards.
If nothing matches, draw one card from the pile. Play it right away if it fits, otherwise your turn passes.
win: Call UNO when you are down to two cards and about to play one of them.
You win the moment your last card leaves your hand.
In a two-player room the game also ends if your rival leaves the room.

othello.title: Othello Guide
othello.goal: Own more discs than your rival on the eight by eight board when the game ends.
play: The board starts with four discs in the middle, two yours and two your rival's.
Place a disc on an empty square so a line of rival discs is trapped between your new disc and one you already own.
Every trapped disc flips to your colour, along rows, columns and diagonals alike.
Legal squares are marked with a yellow dot; a square that traps nothing cannot be played.
If you have no legal move your turn is skipped automatically and your rival plays again.
win: The game ends when neither player has a legal move, usually once the board is full.
Whoever owns more discs at that moment wins, and an equal count is a draw.
Corners are precious because a disc in a corner can never be flipped back.

chess.title: Chess Guide
chess.goal: Attack the enemy king until it has no way out, which is checkmate.
play: White moves first, then both players alternate one move at a time.

Each piece moves its own way: pawns step forward and capture diagonally, rooks go straight, bishops go diagonally, the queen does both, knights jump in an L, and the king steps one square any direction.
An enemy piece standing on your destination square is captured and leaves the board.
Castling tucks the king away by moving it two squares towards a rook, as long as neither has moved and the path is safe.
A pawn that reaches the far rank is promoted, usually to a queen.
win: You win when the enemy king is in check and no move can save it.
The game is drawn when the player to move has no legal move but is not in check, or when too little material is left to checkmate.
In a two-player room the game also ends if your rival leaves the room.

gomoku.title: Gomoku Guide
gomoku.goal: Be the first to line up five of your stones on the fifteen by fifteen board.
play: Players take turns placing one stone on any empty point.
A placed stone is never moved and can never be captured.
The stone you played last is ringed so the sequence is easy to follow.
Watch your rival's rows of three and four, and block an open end before it becomes five.
Playing near the centre gives you more directions to build a row.
win: You win as soon as five of your stones sit in a row, a column, or a diagonal.
The winning line is highlighted in red when the game ends.
If the whole board fills up with no line of five, the game is a draw.

dotsAndBoxes.title: Dots & Box Guide
dotsAndBoxes.goal: Claim the most boxes on a five by five grid of dots that holds sixteen boxes.
play: Players take turns drawing one line between two neighbouring dots.
Lines run horizontally or vertically, and a line that is already drawn cannot be reused.
A box becomes yours when you draw its fourth side; your boxes are marked A and your rival's are marked B.
Closing a box earns you another turn, so several boxes can fall in a row.
Avoid drawing the third side of a box, because your rival only has to close it.
win: The game ends once every line on the board has been drawn.
Whoever owns more boxes wins, and an equal count is a draw.
Long chains of boxes usually decide the result, so choose carefully when you must open one.

game2048.title: 2048 Guide
game2048.goal: Merge matching numbers until a tile reaches 2048.
play: The four by four board starts with two tiles worth 2 or 4.
Swipe up, down, left or right; every tile slides as far as it can in that direction.
Two tiles of the same value that collide merge into one tile of double the value, and that value is added to your score.
A tile can only merge once per swipe, so four equal tiles become two pairs.
Every swipe that changes the board spawns one new tile worth 2, occasionally 4.
win: You win the moment a tile reaches 2048, and you may keep playing afterwards.
The game ends when the board is full and no pair can be merged any more.
Keep your biggest tile in one corner and order the numbers downwards from it so the board does not lock up.
